assessment.nobel_worthiness: A concrete invention with a clear discovery narrative: the optical lattice clock, using a magic wavelength so that many atoms are interrogated Doppler- and recoil-free, now reaching fractional uncertainties near 10^-18. It opens a new regime of precision measurement, enabling tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. Measurement physics of this kind fits the 'discovery or invention' criterion well.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated it early; Ye's group drove the strontium lattice clocks to the 10^-18 level with ultrastable lasers and extensive systematics control. Two laureates give a clean and defensible configuration. Other groups (e.g. at NIST/JILA and elsewhere, Lemonde, Derevianko and others) contributed, but the supplied credit supports a fair two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed in several laboratories and several species; the interpretation is stable and the field is mature. Recognition is timely, and the earlier prize for frequency combs (2005) does not overlap with the lattice-clock concept.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as sufficiently distinct from the earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock recognition.
Precise priority for the magic-wavelength idea relative to contemporaneous proposals is from my recollection and not independently verified here.
A redefinition of the SI second has not yet happened, so the full practical impact is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform in which flat moire bands produce correlated insulators, superconductivity and related phases from a simple carbon system. It is original, conceptually clear and has spawned a large field of twistronics and moire quantum matter. As a materials and interface experimentalist I value that the discovery rests on controlled assembly of atomically thin layers and is confirmed by transport, scanning probes and spectroscopy.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators (including Cao and co-workers) observed correlated insulating and superconducting states in 2018. A theory-plus-experiment prize is natural, but the experimental credit is shared with students and collaborators, and others (e.g. Dean, Young, Yacoby, Efetov and others) made major follow-up contributions, so the line is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Observed in many independent groups since 2018; the phenomenology is broadly confirmed, though the mechanism of superconductivity and the nature of correlated states remain debated. Recognition may be slightly early but not premature on the core discovery.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and the full phase diagram are unresolved.
Whether the committee prefers a prize defined narrowly around the magic-angle prediction and observation, or one that includes broader moire and heterostructure physics.
Allocation of experimental credit beyond Jarillo-Herrero is uncertain; I rely on recollection of the 2011 and 2018 papers and have not verified the author lists here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correction of spherical (and chromatic) aberration in electron lenses overcame a limit recognised since Scherzer's 1936 theorem and delivered sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy in TEM and STEM. It is a clear invention with a decisive and lasting impact across materials physics, nanoscience and chemistry, and it is a direct precedent line from Ruska's 1986 prize for the electron microscope. I should state openly that this is my own field, so I may weigh its technical depth more heavily than colleagues would, and I would expect the committee to test that.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theory and designs of correctors, Haider and colleagues realised the first working TEM corrector, and Krivanek led the STEM corrector. The usual public credit group also includes Knut Urban (Juelich), who is not among the supplied names, so a fair configuration within three names leaves a real credit gap. Several of these people have already shared other major awards, which supports their standing but does not resolve the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Aberration-corrected instruments have been routine for over a decade and results are independently reproduced worldwide; maturity is high. If anything the timing risk is that the invention is old enough to be seen as infrastructure, and that some may consider it chemistry or instrumentation rather than physics.
uncertainties: Exclusion of Knut Urban from the supplied credited names weakens any three-person configuration.
Disciplinary fit (physics versus chemistry) and potential perception of bias because of my own microscopy background; I would recuse myself from advocacy if a concrete conflict applied.
Credit details between the TEM and STEM correctors are from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect are a conceptual advance that created a new class of quantum matter and a prediction-and-experiment success story. The idea extends well beyond the original system and underlies later work on topological materials, edge transport and spin-orbit effects, and the field has strong lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele introduced the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall idea in graphene; Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe quantum wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. The supplied names omit Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and others (Fu, Hasan, Moore, Balents for 3D topological insulators) also contributed, so the allocation is contested and a compound discovery may need different recognition for 2D and 3D cases.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation, including ARPES and transport in many materials, and the interpretation is stable. The 2016 prize for topological phase transitions and matter in part precedes this work but covers different physics, so timing is acceptable.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would treat 2D quantum spin Hall and 3D topological insulators as one discovery.
The Kane-Mele graphene realisation is not practically observable because spin-orbit coupling is small, which may be seen as a weakness of the original proposal.
Credit omitted from the supplied list (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) cannot be assigned here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The LHC and its two general-purpose detectors are among the largest feats of experimental physics and enabled the Higgs discovery and a broad precision programme. The design and construction represent an invention-level contribution, and detector and accelerator developments have affected many fields.
assessment.attribution: Evans led the machine construction; Della Negra and Jenni were central founding figures of CMS and ATLAS respectively. The work is the product of thousands of people, and any three-person selection involves strong simplifications; the Higgs discovery itself is covered in a separate candidate entry with different credited names, which may overlap and creates an allocation ambiguity.
assessment.maturity: Mature and thoroughly confirmed. The Higgs boson theory was recognised in 2013, and recognition of the experimental side is plausibly overdue but remains difficult because of collaboration size.
uncertainties: Fair attribution among accelerator, detector and analysis leaders in huge collaborations.
Overlap with the separate Higgs-discovery candidate, which would have to be resolved to avoid double treatment.
Whether a prize for construction rather than a physics discovery fits the criterion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in IceCube, followed by the identification of TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane as sources, established neutrino astronomy in a way that was unusual in design: a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice. This is an original instrument-driven discovery with lasting scientific impact.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the principal driving scientist for IceCube and Spiering a long-standing leader of the Antarctic neutrino detector efforts. The collaboration is large, and others (e.g. AMANDA pioneers and early proponents of deep-ice neutrino detection) have a claim, so a two-person prize leaves unresolved credit.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is well established; source identification is still developing and individual source associations rest on modest significance. Recognition could be slightly early for the astronomy part but the detector and discovery are firm.
uncertainties: Whether source evidence is mature enough to treat the field as established rather than emerging.
Credit to early pioneers of deep-ice and deep-water neutrino detection is not captured by the supplied names.
KM3NeT and other results may alter the picture; details are not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum anomalous Hall effect gives a quantised Hall conductance without an external magnetic field in a magnetic topological insulator, which is a decisive realisation of a Chern insulator that was conceptually anticipated by Haldane. It is a clear, measurable discovery with fundamental and metrological relevance, building on the topological-materials theme.
assessment.attribution: Fang and Dai with colleagues predicted the effect in Cr- or Fe-doped Bi2Se3-family materials, and Xue's group first observed the quantised plateau in thin films made by molecular beam epitaxy in 2013. Haldane's 1988 model and earlier proposals are antecedents, and others contributed to material growth and later improvements, so the credit is plausible but not exhaustive.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in other laboratories, but the quantisation temperature remains low and precision is still being improved. Recognition is reasonable but may be a few years early relative to the topological-insulator discovery.
uncertainties: Priority relative to Haldane's model and the overlap with the topological-insulator prize question.
Quantisation is observed only at very low temperatures, limiting current practical impact.
Contribution of other theoretical groups to the magnetic topological insulator proposal is not checked here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Horizon-scale imaging of the shadow of M87* and Sagittarius A* is an extraordinary measurement combining mm-VLBI, precision calibration and image reconstruction, giving direct visual evidence of strong-field gravity. It is of broad public and scientific interest and is a coherent observational discovery rather than an incremental one.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed shadow imaging of the Galactic Centre black hole, Doeleman led the early mm-VLBI feasibility and the EHT effort, and Moran contributed long-baseline interferometry foundations. The result was produced by a collaboration of several hundred people, and the individual attribution is difficult and contested, which weakens a fair three-person prize.
assessment.maturity: The 2019 and 2022 results have been reproduced through multiple analysis pipelines and epochs, and polarisation results add confidence, but the interpretation of detailed images and spin remains evolving. Timing is acceptable although the field is still maturing.
uncertainties: Fair allocation of credit given the large collaboration and distributed imaging contributions.
Image-reconstruction dependence and the interpretation of black-hole parameters remain subject to refinement.
Who among the proposers and instrument builders was decisive is from my recollection and not verified.
